name: PRTG - Notification Command Injection (CVE-2018-9276)
description: Authenticated PRTG lets you create a notification that runs a program; the parameter field is command-injectable, so appending shell commands adds a local admin user (PRTG runs as SYSTEM).

defense.why_it_works: PRTG's notification system allows admins to execute programs when alerts fire. The parameter field for the EXE/script notification is unsanitized, enabling OS command injection via semicolons appended after the filename.
defense.prerequisites: Valid PRTG admin credentials (default prtgadmin:prtgadmin often unchanged). Access to PRTG web interface. Ability to create/modify notifications and trigger them.
defense.impact: OS command execution as PRTG service account (often SYSTEM on Windows). Can create local admin users, install backdoors, run Mimikatz -- full Windows host compromise.
defense.detection: PRTG notification creation or modification. Unusual child process from PRTGServer.exe (net.exe, whoami.exe). Windows Security Event 4688 for process creation from PRTG. New local admin account (4720/4732).
defense.artifacts: PRTG audit log (notification modified) | Windows Security Event 4688 (net.exe from PRTG) | Windows Event 4720/4732 (new admin user) | EDR: PRTG spawning cmd.exe
defense.prevention: Change default PRTG credentials immediately. Restrict PRTG web interface to internal IPs. Apply PRTG patches. Run PRTG service as a non-admin service account. Monitor for new local admin account creation.
defense.misconfiguration: PRTG running with default credentials. Service runs as SYSTEM. Notification system allows semicolon-injected OS commands without sanitization.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# PRTG default
# Service account: SYSTEM
# Credentials: prtgadmin:prtgadmin
# Notification param: 'test.txt;net user admin Pwn3d! /add'
# No input sanitization
defense.secure_config:
# Change default credentials immediately
# Run PRTG as low-privilege service account:
New-LocalUser -Name "prtg_svc" -Password (ConvertTo-SecureString "StrongPass!" -AsPlainText -Force)
# Alert on Windows Event 4732 (member added to Administrators)
defense.evasion: Trigger via legitimate alert threshold rather than Test button to avoid direct admin action in audit trail.
